items.title: Argentina reportedly already has first opponent for November window after Lionel Messi’s retirement
items.description:
Costa Rica is reportedly set to be Argentina’s first opponent in the November window, the first since Lionel Messi’s retirement from the national team. 
Argentina reportedly already has its first opponent after the retirement of Lionel Messi from the national team. Costa Rica is expected to be one of the teams that Lionel Scaloni’s side faces during the November international window, although the Argentine Football Association has not announced anything yet and the information comes from outside the country.



According to Costa Rican journalist Kevin Jimenez, the Ticos have already lined up two games in November, to be played in South America, against Argentina and Ecuador. The report comes after Argentina’s plans changed, as a tour of Asia that would have included matches against Saudi Arabia and India has fallen through, leaving the AFA searching for new opponents.



Scaloni had already hinted at the limited options when speaking after the last window, which included matches against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin, the farewell opponent for Messi at the Monumental on Oct. 6.



The coach explained that the teams still available in November were limited, and that while he would like to face powerful opponents, the calendar did not leave much room to choose. 




Costa Rica enfrentará a Argentina y Ecuador en los amistosos de noviembre, serán en Sudamérica 🇨🇷 pic.twitter.com/jkWuE9W9xa— Kevin Jiménez (@KevinJimenezCR) October 14, 2026




The window runs from Nov. 9 to Nov. 17, and Scaloni plans to use the matches to test variations and give young players a chance as he rebuilds a team that finished as runner-up at the 2026 World Cup.


        


Uruguay also emerges as a possible opponent



Costa Rica is not the only name in the discussion. Other reports point to Uruguay, coached by Diego Forlan, as another leading candidate, with matches in La Plata or La Bombonera and even a possible rematch in Montevideo, so the final schedule could still change.



Uruguay arrive at the window after completing a tour of Asia, where Forlan’s side beat South Korea and India but lost to Japan. A meeting with Argentina would be a demanding test for Scaloni, given the intensity that has historically defined the Southamerican rivalry, and it would also give the new generation a chance to prove itself in the first matches of the post-Messi era.

items.title: Turrientes, vini, vidi y casi vinci
items.description: El fútbol suele tener un sentido de la justicia poético, y batallas como la vivida por Beñat Turrientes en Lovaina justifican por qué este deporte rehúsa cualquier lógica pasada. En la víspera del duelo continental frente al Union Saint-Gilloise, Pellegrino Matarazzo lanzó un mensaje directo y sin anestesia hacia su medular: "Turrientes tiene calidad y nos da la estructura de ataque: puede ser un buen jugador, pero se lo tiene que creer con el corazón. Yangel y Soler lo están haciendo bien. Cuando salgan y compitan -él y Gorrotxa-, tienen que hacerlo mejor". Un toque de atención público en toda regla para un futbolista que, tras ser indiscutible el pasado curso, ha visto reducida su presencia de forma drástica en el inicio de la 2026/27. "Hablo a menudo con Turri sobre lo que quiero ver, seguro que escuchó el mensaje ayer, es suficiente. Fue una buena reacción hoy", dijo después del encuentro.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Princess of Asturias Award trip could put his Inter Miami return vs Red Bull New York in doubt
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s trip to Spain for the Princess of Asturias Award could complicate his availability for Inter Miami’s match against Red Bull New York on Oct. 24. 
Lionel Messi is set to travel to Spain next week to receive the Princess of Asturias Award for Sports, and the trip could complicate his availability for Inter Miami’s visit to Red Bull New York on Oct. 24. 



The schedule is tight, with the awards ceremony in Oviedo taking place the day before the match, and although there is no indication that Messi will miss the game, the logistics leave his participation as a possibility to watch.



According to Inter Miami insider José Armando, Messi would arrive in Oviedo on Oct. 22 and take part in the afternoon in a meeting with people from the city, as part of the awards week program. The ceremony itself is scheduled for Oct. 23 at the Teatro Campoamor, where Messi will be honored as one of the most successful players in history.



That timeline leaves little room for the return trip. Inter Miami host Red Bull New York in Harrison, New Jersey, on Oct. 24 at 5:30 p.m. ET, less than a day after the ceremony in Spain, and the journey across the Atlantic could affect how Messi arrives for the match.



Lionel Messi celebrates a goal for Inter Miami. (Getty Images)



The situation comes at a favorable moment for Inter Miami, who clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs with a 2-0 win over NYCFC, a match in which Messi provided an assist. The result moved them to second in the Eastern Conference with 52 points, and the team still has the visit to Atlanta United on Oct. 17 before the match in New Jersey, so any decision on Messi’s workload will likely depend on how the next few days play out.


        


Ballon d’Or gala adds another variable



Another event on the calendar adds to the uncertainty. The Ballon d’Or gala takes place on Oct. 26 at the London Palladium, two days after the match in New Jersey, and although Messi’s attendance has not been confirmed, it is another factor in how he might manage his schedule.



If he decides to travel to London after the match, he would face a second long trip in less than a week, which could make Inter Miami more cautious about how many minutes to give him against Red Bull New York. The club has not commented on any plan for his workload, so for now the possibility remains speculative.



Between the award in Oviedo, the match against Red Bull New York and a possible trip to London for the Ballon d’Or gala, Messi faces one of the busiest weeks of his season, and Inter Miami will have to weigh his schedule against their push in the Eastern Conference. 



Nothing has been confirmed, and his declared intention is to return in time to play, but the decision on whether he starts, comes off the bench or sits out will likely come only once the trip is closer.

items.title: 1-1: La Real trata de controlar y termina perdiendo dos puntos en el 88'
items.description: La Real de Matarazzo continúa sin sentirse del todo cómoda sin la locura ofensiva que le caracteriza y, sobre todo, continúa sufriendo una barbaridad gestionando ventajas. Los txuri urdin se dejaron dos puntos de oro en Bélgica ante el Union Saint-Gilloise en el 88', que le complican sobremanera ya pensar en el top 8 de la fase de liga de la Europa League salvo machada. El conjunto realista fue diferente, se intentó adaptar al contexto y al rival, a los diferentes tiempos del encuentro, buscó el control tras ponerse por delante con el gol del revulsivo inmediato Turrientes, que pasaran pocas cosas, lo estaba consiguiendo pero defendió mal una falta lateral que le condenó. Aunque fue aún más cruel el final con el gol salvado de manera milagrosa por Sylla, sobre la bocina. Uno de seis en Europa, obligación de ganar en Noruega el jueves que viene. Pero primero, Málaga.

items.title: Is Christian Pulisic playing today? Confirmed lineups for RB Salzburg vs AC Milan in Matchday 2 of the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for RB Salzburg vs AC Milan in the 2026-27 UEFA Europa League. Salzburg host Milan in the Europa League with both sides looking to build on contrasting midweek results.
RB Salzburg come into this one off the back of a 1-0 win over Levski Sofia on September 17, and Danny Rohl’s side will look to carry that result into a tougher continental test.
AC Milan, meanwhile, are still digesting a 0-2 loss to Benfica on September 16, and Ruben Amorim needs a response from his group on the road.
As for Christian Pulisic, the forward is expected to start from the bench as AC Milan coach Ruben Amorin is set to rotate the lineup to rest starters and give more minutes to other players.
RB Salzburg confirmed lineup
Rohl sets Salzburg up in a 4-2-3-1, with Christian Fruchtl behind a back four of Schmid, Boma, Kratzig and Lainer. Kitano and Mazurek sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Barry, Vertessen and Baidoo who support lone striker Tabakovic. The setup favors quick transitions through the wide areas, with Baidoo and Vertessen tasked with stretching Milan’s back line.
RB Salzburg confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Christian Zawieschitzky, Dominik Robin Schmid, Kevin Boma, Leandro Morgalla, Valentin Zabransky, Sota Kitano, Bartosz Mazurek, Abubakr Barry, Haris Tabakovic, Edmund Baidoo, Jesper Lindstrom. Coach: Danny Rohl.
AC Milan confirmed lineup
Amorim lines Milan up in a 3-4-2-1, with Maignan behind a back three of Pavlovic, De Winter and Tomori. Pulisic and Bartesaghi operate as the wide outlets in a four-man midfield alongside Modric and Chukwueze, with Cisse and Musah pushed up to support Camarda at the point of the attack. Modric’s presence in the middle gives Milan control of possession, while Loftus-Cheek and Chukwueze provide the width to test Salzburg’s full backs.
AC Milan confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Mike Maignan, Strahinja Pavlovic, Koni De Winter, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Davide Bartesaghi, Adrien Rabiot, Omari Hutchinson, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda. Coach: Ruben Amorim.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s sister singles out the biggest obstacle to Portugal return and Jorge Jesus reconciliation in emotional statement
items.description:
Her latest comments have raised fresh questions about whether the Al-Nassr forward will return to the national team, as the disagreement threatens to leave a lasting mark on one of the most significant relationships in Portuguese soccer. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s international future has become increasingly uncertain after his sister, Elma Aveiro, made an emotional statement about the ongoing dispute between the Portugal captain and head coach Jorge Jesus. Her latest comments have raised fresh questions about whether the Al-Nassr forward will return to the national team, as the disagreement threatens to leave a lasting mark on one of the most significant relationships in Portuguese soccer.



Speaking to reporters in Lisbon on Wednesday, Elma expressed sadness over the way her brother has been treated and questioned whether the situation could be resolved. Her remarks followed Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal’s training camp during the recent UEFA Nations League window, an incident that triggered disciplinary proceedings and intensified speculation about his international future.



Elma made it clear that the controversy has been difficult for her to watch, particularly given everything Ronaldo has achieved throughout his career. The Selecao captain has spent more than two decades representing his country, becoming its all-time leading goalscorer and helping it win the 2016 Euro and the 2019 UEFA Nations League.



“My position is one of sadness. Unfortunately, the Portuguese people forget what people do and what they have already achieved. Now, they think the present should be different,” Elma said.



“Je pense qu’il (Cristiano) ne veut plus rejouer pour la sélection. Il y a plus de chances qu’il ne revienne pas, que l’inverse.”— Elma Aveiro, sœur de CR7 pic.twitter.com/H10DMJfO2X— As Quinas 🇵🇹 (@AsQuinasOff) October 14, 2026



She also admitted that seeing her brother caught in the middle of the dispute had left her struggling to find the right words. “I was even left speechless because it’s complicated. It’s very complicated to see my brother go through this because, of all people, he was one of the least deserving of it.”



Elma reveals the biggest obstacle to reconciliation



When asked directly whether Ronaldo wanted to return to Portugal, Elma offered a pessimistic assessment that could worry supporters hoping for a swift resolution. “I don’t think so,” she replied when questioned about his desire to come back.



She subsequently expanded on her answer, suggesting that the dispute had reached an impasse because of the emotions involved on both sides. “I believe it’s more likely that he won’t than that he will. I think they’re both hurt. It’s a situation they experienced themselves, not me. I can only speak on behalf of my brother, and I think things are at a standstill at the moment. We’ll see how it turns out.”



Her most revealing comment came when the discussion turned to whether Ronaldo and Jesus could eventually make peace. “I don’t know. It’s very complicated. You know something? When you’ve been betrayed, it’s difficult to go back to how things were before.” Elma’s reference to betrayal highlights the central obstacle facing any potential reconciliation: rebuilding trust after a disagreement that has become public and deeply personal.



Elma Aveiro traz más notícias para os portugueses. pic.twitter.com/eE0Drt6kQx— Cabine Desportiva (@CabineSport) October 14, 2026



Will Ronaldo return to Portugal in November?



Despite the uncertainty surrounding Portugal, Elma offered reassurance about her brother’s condition and his return to club soccer. She confirmed that the 41-year-old was back playing for Al-Nassr and described his physical and mental state as good.



“He’s doing well and has already returned to playing with Al-Nassr. His physical condition is good, as is his mental state,” she explained. However, she acknowledged that the controversy has affected him to some extent, adding that her brother continues to overcome difficulties because “he’s a great man.”



Head coach Jorge Jesus interacts with Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr. (Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)



Jesus has previously indicated that the door remains open for Ronaldo to return, emphasizing that the decision ultimately belongs to the player. The November international window, when Portugal is scheduled to face Denmark and Wales, could allow both sides to move forward.



However, Elma’s comments suggest that a return may require more than simply resolving the disciplinary matter. Ronaldo would need to decide whether he is ready to resume working under Jesus, while the coach and federation would need to find a way to restore confidence after the breakdown in their relationship.

items.title: Internacional Sub-15 del Barça y árbitro
items.description: El FC Barcelona fichó el pasado verano para la categoría cadete de su fútbol base a un talento gallego pretendido por otras grandes canteras de España como las de Real Madrid y Atlético de Madrid: Gael José Seijo, central de 14 años que también puede jugar de mediocentro. Natural de Taboada (Luego), llegó tras jugar dos años en el infantil del Deportivo y ser internacional Sub-14, aunque se formó en el CD Lugo desde muy niño. En un reportaje de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) con motivo de la concentración de la selección española Sub-15 explica con desparpajo una curiosidad: su pasión por el arbitraje que ya ejercía con titulación en Galicia. Aunque en La Masia se ha tenido que centrar en su condición de futbolista, se guarda para el futuro la posibilidad de ser árbitro profesional.

items.title: Catalá: "Tenemos un pedazo de grupo, somos una familia"
items.description: José Luis Catalá está siendo una gran alternativa en defensa para el Sabadell en este inicio de temporada. Llegó este verano y asegura haberse adaptado rápidamente gracias al ambiente que ha encontrado en el vestuario: “La adaptación con el pedazo de grupo que tenemos, la familia, ha sido muy fácil gracias al míster y staff", ha explicado hoy en rueda de prensa. Y aunque quizás no está contando con todos los minutos que le gustaría, asegura estar "preparado para lo que sea, para cuando el míster me ponga, darlo todo, y dar el máximo siempre”. Entre otras cosas, ha insistido en la necesidad de mantener los pies en el suelo y pensar únicamente en el próximo partido.

items.title: La calidad de la uva define la vendimia en la Denominación de Origen Toro
items.description: La campaña de vendimia en la Denominación de Origen Toro llega a su fin con un balance positivo. Las 54 bodegas adscritas al Consejo Regulador han recibido aproximadamente 19,9 millones de kilos de uva, una cifra ligeramente inferior a los 21 millones de kilos que suele registrar habitualmente la zona. Sin embargo, el resultado ha superado las previsiones iniciales y se sitúa en niveles muy similares a los de la campaña anterior. «Pensábamos que la producción iba a ser alrededor de un 10% inferior a la del año pasado, pero finalmente la cifra será muy similar», explica Santiago Castro, ingeniero agrónomo y máster en Enología y Viticultura, que ocupa desde 2005 el cargo de director técnico del Consejo Regulador de la Denominación de Origen Toro.

items.title: FA spending on Wembley hospitality and free tickets for FA Council rises by 25%
items.description: Expenditure rises to £564,000 in 2025-26 seasonCost of hosting FA Council meetings also almost doublesThe Football Association spent 25% more on Wembley hospitality and freebies for FA Council members last season, the Guardian can reveal. The latest accounts show expenditure on tickets and hospitality rose from £452,300 in the 2024-25 season to £564,400 in 2025-26.While fans across the country have staged protests and walkouts in recent years over ticket price rises, and the cost-of-living crisis has made football increasingly unaffordable, the FA has upgraded the hospitality it offers to VIPs. items.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
items.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the clubHeartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season, given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence.For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. items.title: Vinicius Junior speaks out on Endrick substitution in Real Madrid’s 4-3 Roma comeback
items.description:
The decisive turning point in Real Madrid's 4–3 comeback win over AS Roma occurred in the 58th minute at the Stadio Olimpico, when manager Jose Mourinho substituted Vinicius Junior and brought on 20-year-old Brazilian forward Endrick. 
Real Madrid were struggling against Roma in Matchday 2 of the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League, but the momentum shifted dramatically when Vinicius Junior came off the pitch for Endrick.



At the 58th minute of the match at the Stadio Olimpico, Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho decided to substitute Vinicius Junior. The Brazilian was enduring a difficult outing, and the coach opted to inject fresh energy into the attack to reverse a 3–1 deficit.



Endrick entered the match and completely changed the dynamic for Los Blancos. The 20-year-old forward spearheaded the historic 4–3 comeback victory, earning Man of the Match honors despite playing only 32 minutes off the bench.



Vinicius Junior reflects on his performance and the Endrick substitution



Vinicius Junior is undeniably navigating one of the most challenging stretches of his career. However, he remains acutely aware that soccer is a team sport; despite being withdrawn early, he celebrated the collective result and praised Endrick’s decisive display.



Vinicius Jr. of Real Madrid.



“It was normal [to be unhappy with the change]. I want to play all minutes and help the team, but it’s not possible,” Vini said after the game. “Endrick came on and changed the match. He was the best player in the 2nd half. We hope he continues to develop, Carlos Espi too.”


        


Ever since missing out on the 2024 Ballon d’Or, Vinicius has struggled to recapture his top level. While the setback took a significant toll on him, the winger has pledged that he is working tirelessly to regain his confidence and return to his peak form.

items.title: Real Madrid stage historic 4-3 Champions League comeback over Roma with stunning late blitz
items.description:
Real Madrid reminded European soccer never to take them for granted, writing another unforgettable chapter in UEFA Champions League history with a sensational 4–3 comeback victory against AS Roma at the Stadio Olimpico. 
Trailing 3–1 with barely eight minutes remaining, Jose Mourinho’s side mounted a furious late blitz to leave Rome with a stunning 4–3 victory, marking another historic night for Real Madrid in the UEFA Champions League.



After a difficult opening hour, Real Madrid found themselves trailing 3–1 with less than ten minutes remaining. However, they scored three consecutive goals in rapid succession to secure all three points away from home.



The comeback began in the 82nd minute courtesy of Carlos Espi, followed by strikes from Endrick and Antonio Rudiger to stun Roma and snatch the victory away from the Italian hosts.



A Historic Night for Real Madrid



According to Spanish statistician MisterChip, Real Madrid’s comeback against Roma in the 2026–27 UEFA Champions League is the fastest away comeback by any team from two goals down in tournament history.



Federico Valverde of Real Madrid.



The record was previously held by Liverpool, who overturned a 2–0 deficit against Villarreal in May 2022 by scoring three goals in 12 minutes and 48 seconds to reach the final.   


        


This time, Real Madrid accomplished the feat in just 7 minutes and 43 seconds, shattering Liverpool’s previous mark. Beyond claiming the three points, they wrote yet another unforgettable chapter in a competition they know better than anyone.



A Breath of Fresh Air for Real Madrid



Facing a demanding fixture run, Real Madrid desperately needed this morale boost. The club will take on Sevilla and Barcelona next in La Liga—two high-stakes matchups that could significantly shape their domestic campaign.



The clash in Rome was anything but simple, and the Italian side proved it by keeping Real Madrid down 3–1 late into the second half. However, this thrilling comeback win provides precisely the momentum and breathing room Los Blancos need as they head into pivotal fixtures ahead.

items.title: Mourinho slams Spanish referees’ committee over Vinicius Junior’s four-match ban
items.description:
The Spanish Football Federation's (RFEF) Disciplinary Committee has officially handed Vinicius Junior a four-match domestic suspension, and Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho believes the timing of the announcement was off. 
Vinicius Junior will officially miss El Clasico against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation’s (RFEF) Disciplinary Committee handed him a four-game suspension. Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho reacted strongly to the news with critical remarks directed toward the governing body.



The announcement of Vini Jr.’s suspension arrived just before Real Madrid’s UEFA Champions League clash against Roma. The timing was openly questioned by Mourinho, who expressed frustration that such a verdict was publicized right before a major European fixture.



“Ask Spanish Refereeing Committee why they published the news about Vini’s ban minutes before he plays an important UCL game,” Mourinho said prior the game against the Italian club. “Real Madrid is a Spanish club, so why publish it now?”



The suspension was more severe than expected



Initial reports suggested that Vinicius Junior would face a two-game ban after pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair and arguing with the match officials.


        


However, the referee’s detailed report prompted a much harsher sanction, and the Brazilian winger was ultimately handed a four-game suspension. Consequently, his absence will extend well beyond just El Clasico.



Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid (2026)



Vinicius will be sidelined for upcoming La Liga fixtures against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing de Santander, and Valencia. While Real Madrid are expected to appeal the ruling, it appears unlikely that the committee will reduce the penalty.



Vinicius Junior is facing a tough 2026–27 season



In the match against Villarreal, Vinicius appeared to have scored to put Real Madrid 2–0 ahead. However, a VAR review revealed his previous foul on Saliba, leading to the goal being disallowed and a straight red card being issued.



It has been an unfortunate series of events for Vini, who is experiencing one of his most challenging starts to a campaign in recent years. Nevertheless, this enforced break may offer him the opportunity to reset, regroup, and return with a renewed mentality for the remainder of the season.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe scores in 100th Champions League game to move past Raul and enter the all-time top five
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe scores in his 100th Champions League appearance to pass Raul and move into fifth place on the all-time list. 
Kylian Mbappe marked his 100th Champions League appearance with a goal at the Stadio Olimpico, and in doing so moved past Raul into fifth place on the competition’s all-time scoring list. The French forward equalized for Real Madrid against Roma in the first half, taking his career tally to 72 goals in the tournament.



The goal ended a tie with Raul at 71, which Mbappe had carried into the match, and it moves him alone into fifth. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi, Robert Lewandowski and Karim Benzema have scored more in the competition.



His journey to the milestone started with Monaco in 2016-17, when he made his debut as a substitute against Bayer Leverkusen and scored his first goal in a 5-3 loss to Manchester City.



He has since scored in nearly half of his appearances, with four hat-tricks, 11 braces and a four-goal haul against Olympiacos in a 4-3 win. He also reached the 2020 final with Paris Saint-Germain, but the trophy remains the one piece missing from his career.




Champions League all-time top scorers:  1. Cristiano Ronaldo 2. Lionel Messi  3. Robert Lewandowski  4. Karim Benzema  5. Kylian Mbappé   #UCL pic.twitter.com/GFEMCW2jyr— UEFA Champions League (@ChampionsLeague) October 14, 2026




The strike also arrived at a useful moment for Mbappe, whose form had cooled in recent weeks after a strong start to the season. He had scored eight goals across LaLiga and the Champions League before the match, and his scoring touch has been under scrutiny at a Madrid side still searching for consistency under Jose Mourinho, who has defended him publicly.


        


Champions League all-time top scorers



With his goal in Rome, Mbappe sits alone in fifth place with 72 goals, one clear of Raul and behind only four players who have defined the competition’s scoring history. Ronaldo, Messi, Lewandowski and Benzema still hold the top four spots, while Harry Kane and Thomas Muller are tied for 10th after Kane’s brace against Viking.



PlayerGoalsCristiano Ronaldo141Lionel Messi129Robert Lewandowski109Karim Benzema90Kylian Mbappe72Raul71Erling Haaland61Ruud van Nistelrooy60Andriy Shevchenko59Thomas Muller57Harry Kane57



Mbappe’s recent goal is another step toward the very top of the Champions League scoring charts, but he still has a long way to go to catch Benzema, who sits 18 goals ahead in fourth. At 27, he has time to keep climbing, and his place on the list is already secure alongside the biggest names in the competition.

items.title: Why are Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva not starting for Real Madrid vs Roma in the 2026-27 Champions League?
items.description:
Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva start on the bench as José Mourinho keeps Vinícius, Diomande and Bellingham behind Mbappé in Rome. 
Arda Guler and Bernardo Silva are on the bench for Real Madrid’s Champions League clash against Roma, but the decision has nothing to do with an injury. José Mourinho, back at the Stadio Olimpico where he led Roma to Conference League glory in 2022, has opted for a more physical midfield, leaving the two creative players among the substitutes.



Both were eligible again after serving suspensions, but neither has had much of a role recently. Bernardo started three of Madrid’s first five LaLiga games, but he has played only 8 minutes in the league since Sept. 12, as Mourinho leaned on Aurélien Tchouaméni and Federico Valverde as his preferred midfield pairing.



Guler is also a victim of a crowded attack. Vinícius Júnior, Yan Diomande and Jude Bellingham start behind Kylian Mbappé, the same trio Mourinho has used in recent matches, and Diomande keeps his place after scoring his first goal for the club in the win over Villarreal.



Madrid have not been convincing since the international break. They edged past Villarreal in a tight game that ended with ten men and they sit six points behind Barcelona in LaLiga. They do arrive in Rome off a 2-1 home win over Inter in their league-phase opener.




📋✅ ¡Nuestro XI inicial! 🆚 @OfficialASRoma pic.twitter.com/5Hm3Ztb4dl— Real Madrid C.F. (@realmadrid) October 14, 2026




Mourinho has not given an official reason for the omissions, so the move reads as a tactical call for a tough away fixture. Güler and Bernardo remain options to change the game from the bench, particularly if Madrid need more control against Gian Piero Gasperini’s back three.


        


Lineups confirmed



Mourinho goes with a 4-2-3-1. Dean Huijsen drops to the bench, with Ibrahima Konaté and Antonio Rudiger forming the center-back pairing and Denzel Dumfries and Marc Cucurella at full-back in front of Thibaut Courtois.



Real Madrid confirmed lineup: Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Rudiger, Cucurella; Tchouaméni, Valverde; Diomande, Bellingham, Vinícius; Mbappé.



Roma line up in their usual 3-4-2-1 and are without goalkeeper Mile Svilar, who is out with a finger injury, so Pierluigi Gollini starts. Paulo Dybala and Matías Soulé play behind Donyell Malen, who is free to play in Europe because his red card against Como only carries a Serie A suspension.



Roma confirmed lineup: Gollini; Mancini, N’Dicka, Hermoso; Molina, De Roon, Koné, Wesley; Dybala, Soulé; Malen.

items.description: Liverpool cleansed themselves from the stains of defeat by Manchester City at the earliest opportunity. A rampant display in Austria saw Bradley Barcola ignite his Liverpool account with the first hat-trick of his professional career and Andoni Iraola’s team devastate Lask’s big night in the Champions League. The major surprise was how the hosts managed to score three.Iraola’s pre-match faith in the big-money signings Barcola and Florian Wirtz was repaid as the pair helped dismantle limited opponents. But it was not all about the money and the £123m signing from Paris Saint-Germain scoring the first goals of his Liverpool career. Lewis Koumas registered his first goal in the competition and replaced Steven Gerrard as the youngest player to score and assist in a Champions League game for Liverpool. items.title: Vinicius to miss El Clasico showdown vs Barcelona after La Liga confirms four-game ban as key reason for double punishment revealed
items.description:
The decision represents a significant setback for Jose Mourinho’s side, which must navigate a demanding run of domestic fixtures without one of its most important attacking players. 
Vinicius Junior will miss Real Madrid’s crucial El Clasico clash against Barcelona after the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) confirmed a four-match La Liga suspension following his controversial dismissal against Villarreal. The decision represents a significant setback for Jose Mourinho’s side, which must navigate a demanding run of domestic fixtures without one of its most important attacking players.



The Brazilian was sent off during Real Madrid’s 1-0 victory over the Yellow Submarine after a VAR review identified an incident involving Nathan Saliba. Although Yan Diomande’s first goal for the club secured three valuable points, Vinicius’ red card quickly became the main talking point, with the punishment now threatening to affect Madrid’s title ambitions.



Vinicius entered the Villarreal match as a substitute after returning from international duty with Brazil, having travelled to Australia and India during the break. He initially appeared to have doubled Madrid’s lead after Jude Bellingham delivered a cutback, but the celebrations ended when the referee reviewed footage of his interaction with Saliba.



The VAR intervention resulted in a straight red card for the Brazilian, with his apparent goal disallowed. Los Blancos subsequently had to protect their narrow advantage with 10 men, eventually holding on for a victory that kept the club six points behind La Liga leader Barcelona.



🇪🇸 | Vinícius Jr. fue expulsado ante Villarreal tras esta acción cuando Real Madrid ganaba 1-0. pic.twitter.com/98RIbmhvSh— Polymarket Español (@polymarketenesp) October 10, 2026 



Why Vinicius received double punishment



The Spanish Football Federation’s Disciplinary Committee ultimately handed Vinicius two separate two-match suspensions, explaining why the punishment reached four games rather than the three-match ban Real Madrid had reportedly anticipated.



The first two matches were imposed for violent conduct away from the play, while the additional two were awarded for protesting against the referee after his dismissal. The committee’s ruling cited Article 130.2 for the violent-conduct sanction and Article 127 for the protests, with additional fines stipulated under Article 52 of the Disciplinary Code.



The official explanation described the first offence as “acting violently away from play, when not in a position to challenge for the ball or when play was stopped.” The second suspension was imposed for “protesting against the referee, assistant referee or fourth official.”



Vue comment il a réagit après le carton rouge on est sûr que c'est le vrai Vinicus et il n'a pas été cloné pic.twitter.com/SS1yzYF2W1— Lamine Galsen 🇸🇳 (@veridique_sn) October 10, 2026 



That distinction is central to understanding the decision. Vinicius was punished both for the original hair-pulling incident and for his conduct after receiving the red card, with the committee treating them as separate disciplinary offences.



Hair-pulling is explicitly classified as violent conduct



The dismissal was also consistent with guidance published by the Spanish Football Federation’s Technical Committee of Referees. Its disciplinary document, known as the CARD, explicitly lists pulling an opponent’s hair among the actions that can constitute violent conduct and warrant a straight red card.



The guidelines state: “A player elbows, headbutts, punches, slaps, grabs an opponent by the neck, pushes, kicks, strikes with the foot, bites, pulls an opponent’s hair, or commits similar acts against an opponent or any other person while not challenging for the ball, using excessive force or brutality.”



According to Mundo Deportivo, the refereeing committee considered the dismissal justified under those guidelines. Vinicius’ reaction afterward then became a separate issue for the Disciplinary Committee, resulting in the additional two-match suspension.



Vinicius Junior of Real Madrid vs Villarreal



Which matches will Vinicius miss?



The suspension rules Vinicius out of Real Madrid’s next four La Liga fixtures: Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Most significantly, the Brazilian will be unavailable for the El Clasico against Barcelona on October 25, potentially depriving Mourinho of a major attacking threat in one of the season’s most important matches.



Vinicius is expected to return to domestic action when Madrid faces Celta Vigo on November 22, following the November international break. He remains eligible to feature in European competition during the suspension, as the ban applies to La Liga matches.



The absence could also create an opportunity for Diomande, whose decisive goal against Villarreal strengthened his case for a more prominent role. With Vinicius already facing scrutiny over his recent performances, the Ivorian winger could benefit if he impresses while the Brazilian is unavailable.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s legal troubles extend beyond Portugal as Juventus steps up five-year financial dispute
items.description:
While the Portugal captain awaits a decision over his departure from the national team camp, his former Italian club has taken another step in a separate case that could have significant financial consequences. 
Cristiano Ronaldo is facing renewed legal uncertainty on two fronts, with disciplinary proceedings in Portugal unfolding alongside a long-running financial dispute involving Juventus. While the Portugal captain awaits a decision over his departure from the national team camp, his former Italian club has taken another step in a separate case that could have significant financial consequences.



The Juventus dispute has already passed through arbitration and a Turin court, with both decisions favoring Ronaldo on the central payment issue. However, the Italian club is refusing to accept the outcome and has appealed to Italy’s Court of Cassation, extending a legal battle that began after his departure in 2021.



The Italian giant confirmed in its 2025-26 financial report that it had appealed to the Court of Cassation, with the appeal formally notified on March 27, 2026. The club is now awaiting a hearing date as it challenges previous decisions requiring it to pay Ronaldo deferred wages from his final season in Turin.



The dispute centers on approximately €19.5 million ($21.7m) in wages that Ronaldo says he was promised during the COVID-19 pandemic. In April 2024, an arbitration panel ruled that Juventus should pay him €9.8 million ($10.9m), plus interest and adjustments, representing roughly half of the amount he originally claimed.



Weston McKennie and Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus F.C. warm up



Juventus subsequently challenged the award, but the Turin Labor Court rejected its appeal in January 2026. According to La Gazzetta della Sport, the club has now taken the case to the country’s highest court of appeal, although the final outcome remains uncertain.



The story behind the ‘Ronaldo Paper’



The controversy dates back to the pandemic, when Juventus and its players discussed arrangements intended to ease the financial pressure caused by the disruption to football. A document associated with Ronaldo, widely known as the “Ronaldo Paper” or “Ronaldo card,” later emerged during the investigation into the club’s financial practices.



The document concerned deferred wages that Ronaldo says remained payable after he left Juventus for Manchester United in 2021. The club has argued that the agreement did not create an enforceable obligation, pointing to the absence of Ronaldo’s signature and maintaining that he did not formally request the money during negotiations over his departure.



The issue attracted further scrutiny during the Prisma investigation, which examined Juventus’s financial reporting and wage arrangements. The wider scandal contributed to the resignation of former president Andrea Agnelli and the club’s board of directors in 2022.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus looks on during the pre-season friendly match.



Why Ronaldo has already won twice



Ronaldo initiated legal proceedings in September 2023, and the dispute proceeded to arbitration because of questions surrounding the recovered document. The panel ruled in his favor by majority in April 2024, awarding him €9.8 million ($10.9m) rather than the approximately €19.5 million ($21.7m) he had sought.



The arbitration panel did not conclude that Juventus had deliberately deceived Ronaldo, and it noted that he had not formally demanded the payment when he left Italy. Nevertheless, the award recognized an obligation to pay the reduced amount, and the Turin Labor Court later rejected Juventus’s challenge.



The club has maintained that the subsequent court decision dealt with procedural defects rather than reassessing the underlying merits of the dispute. In its financial report, Juventus stated: “The decision was limited to a review of the formal defects in the award reported in the appeal, and is not a decision on the merits of the case.”



Cristiano Ronaldo of Juventus celebrates with the TIMVISION cup.



What does Juventus say?



Despite the continuing legal battle, Juventus has sought to reassure shareholders that the dispute will not create a new financial shock. The club says the economic effects of the arbitration award have already been reflected in its accounts since the 2023-24 financial year.



“In any case, the economic and financial effects resulting from the award have already been reflected in the Company’s accounts since the 2023–2024 financial year, and therefore no negative impacts on the current or future financial statements are expected,” the club explained.



That accounting position means Juventus does not expect the ongoing proceedings to create an additional impact on its current or future financial statements. However, the appeal leaves the underlying dispute unresolved until the Court of Cassation considers the case.

items.title: Is Kylian Mbappe playing today? Confirmed lineups for Roma vs Real Madrid in Matchday 2 of 2026-27 UEFA Champions League
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Roma vs Real Madrid in the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League. Roma host Real Madrid at the Stadio Olimpico in a Champions League group clash that pits Gian Piero Gasperini’s back three against Jose Mourinho’s old club in Spain’s capital giants.
Roma go into this one off a 1-1 draw with Fenerbahce on September 10, a result that leaves them still searching for their first win of the European campaign.
Real Madrid arrive on the back of a 2-1 win over Inter on September 8, a result that keeps them unbeaten and gives them momentum heading into Rome. For this game, Kylian Mbappe is expected to start despite the recent knee injury he suffered with France during the international break.
Roma confirmed lineup
Gasperini sets Roma up in a 3-4-2-1 with Gollini behind a back three of Hermoso, Ndicka and Mancini. Wesley Franca and Molina provide width as wing backs either side of Kone and De Roon in central midfield, while Soule and Dybala operate just behind Malen as the central outlet. There are no absences listed for Roma, so Gasperini can pick from a full squad for this test against Madrid’s attack.
Roma confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): Pierluigi Gollini, Nahuel Molina, Wesley, Mario Hermoso, Evan Ndicka, Gianluca Mancini, Marten de Roon, Manu Koné, Donyell Malen, Paulo Dybala, Matías Soulé. Coach: Gian Piero Gasperini.
Real Madrid confirmed lineup
Mourinho lines Real Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1 with Courtois in goal behind a back four of Cucurella, Rudiger, Dumfries and Konate. Bellingham and Valverde anchor the midfield, with Bernardo Silva, Vinicius Junior and Arda Guler supporting Mbappe as the focal point up front. With no absences reported, Mourinho has his full first-choice group available to work with in Rome.
Real Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Thibaut Courtois, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella, Aurélien Tchouaméni, Ibrahima Konaté, Antonio Rüdiger, Yan Diomande, Federico Valverde, Vinícius Júnior, Jude Bellingham, Kylian Mbappé. Coach: José Mário dos Santos Mourinho Félix.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s 2026-27 Saudi Super Cup route is set, but Al-Nassr faces one major obstacle on road to silverware
items.description:
The Portuguese superstar will lead his team into a demanding knockout tournament in December, where one decisive match could determine whether his side gets the chance to compete for the trophy. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr now know what stands between them and another opportunity to lift silverware, following the draw for the 2026-27 Saudi Super Cup. The Portuguese superstar will lead his team into a demanding knockout tournament in December, where one decisive match could determine whether his side gets the chance to compete for the trophy.



The competition will bring together four Saudi clubs in Kuwait, with the semi-finals scheduled for December 19 and 20 before the final takes place on December 23. With no second chances in the knockout format, Al-Nassr will need to deliver when it matters most.



The draw has produced two intriguing semi-final matchups, with Al-Ahli facing Al-Qadsiah on December 19 and Al-Nassr taking on Al-Kholood on December 20. The winners will advance to the final, where the next Saudi Super Cup champion will be crowned.



The tournament will take place at Jaber Al-Ahmad International Stadium in Kuwait, marking the country’s first time hosting the competition. The 13th edition will run from December 19 to 23, with the final scheduled for the tournament’s last day.



في ديرة الأحبة اكتملت القرعة 🇰🇼

ومواجهات نصف النهائي جاهزة 🤩

#السوبر_في_الكويت https://t.co/guz6DHw5NQ— كأس السوبر السعودي (@SaudiSuperCup) October 14, 2026




For Ronaldo and Al-Nassr, the draw offers a clear route to the final, but reaching that stage will require a strong semi-final performance. The club cannot afford to underestimate its opponent, particularly in a competition where a single result can end its pursuit of the trophy.



Who could Ronaldo meet in the final?



The first challenge for Al-Nassr will be Al-Kholood, its semi-final opponent on December 20. Victory would send Ronaldo’s team into the final three days later, keeping its hopes of winning the Saudi Super Cup alive.



That is the obstacle Al-Nassr must overcome before it can turn its attention to the title itself. If Al-Nassr beats Al-Kholood, it will face either Al-Ahli or Al-Qadsiah in the final on December 23, setting up a potentially demanding encounter against another of Saudi soccer’s ambitious clubs.



Al-Ahli and Al-Qadsiah will meet a day earlier to decide the first finalist. Both teams will have the same objective: secure a place in the final and move within one victory of lifting the trophy.



Goalkeeper Edouard Mendy of Al Ahli (C), and other players poses for photo with trophy afte winning the Saudi Super Cup



Kuwait prepares to welcome Saudi’s biggest names



Hosting the tournament represents a significant occasion for Kuwait, which becomes the eighth host in the Saudi Super Cup’s history. The matches will be staged at a venue with a capacity of approximately 60,000, allowing for large crowds across all three fixtures.



The draw ceremony brought together soccer and sporting officials from both countries. Among those attending were Saudi ambassador to Kuwait Prince Sultan bin Saad bin Khalid, Kuwait Football Association president Sheikh Ahmad Al-Yousef Al-Sabah and Kuwaiti sports minister Dr Tareq Al-Jalahma.



For Ronaldo, the immediate objective will be to guide Al-Nassr past Al-Kholood and secure a place in the final. The Portuguese forward has built his career around delivering in decisive moments, but the knockout format leaves little room for mistakes. Al-Nassr needs one semi-final victory to move within reach of the Saudi Super Cup, but a potential final against Al-Ahli or Al-Qadsiah could provide another difficult test.

items.title: Hansi Flick explains why Lamine Yamal played full 90 minutes in Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Galatasaray
items.description:
Barcelona overcame an early deficit to dismantle Galatasaray 4–1 at RAMS Park in Matchday 2 of the UEFA Champions League. Despite opening up a comfortable three-goal cushion in the second half and withdrawing key starters, manager Hansi Flick decided to keep Lamine Yamal on the pitch for the full 90 minutes. 
Barcelona had little trouble defeating Galatasaray on the road. Nevertheless, despite establishing a comfortable advantage, Hansi Flick chose to keep Lamine Yamal on the pitch for the full 90 minutes.



Lamine Yamal finished the match as Man of the Match after delivering two brilliant assists. Without Raphinha on the field, Hansi Flick needed someone to step up as a leader, and he found that spark in the young star.



“Lamine is physically top , and he enjoys playing soccer,” Hansi Flick said about Yamal playing the 90 minutes against Galatasaray. “You saw him in the second half. He changed the game for us.”



Barcelona are in formidable form



Barcelona do not know what it feels like to lose this season—in fact, they have yet to even draw. The Blaugrana have won all of their games across all competitions this campaign, proving why they are currently regarded as leading contenders.



Lamine Yamal of FC Barcelona looks on



The trip to Galatasaray was never going to be easy. Barcelona fell behind early, but they mounted an emphatic comeback to not only win, but crush the Turkish side at a venue renowned as one of the most hostile environments in European soccer.


        


Even without Raphinha, Barcelona are proving they have plenty of dangerous attacking alternatives. Now, a demanding schedule awaits as they prepare to face Real Betis, PSG, and Real Madrid over the next three weeks.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami could book their 2026 MLS Cup playoff ticket against NYCFC
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami can clinch a 2026 MLS Cup playoff berth with a win over New York City FC. 
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami have a chance to secure their place in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs when they host New York City FC. The Herons enter the match in strong form, knowing that a victory would be enough to make the postseason official with the regular season entering its final stretch.



Inter Miami arrive second in the Eastern Conference with 49 points from 28 matches, behind league-leading Nashville SC, who have 63. A win against NYCFC would clinch a playoff spot for Miami, while other results could also seal it if the game ends in a draw.



Miami are coming off a 4-0 rout of D.C. United, a match in which both Messi and Luis Suárez scored braces. Inter Miami will lean on their explosive attack, led by Messi, who has 23 goals and 11 assists this season, while Suárez has 15 goals.



NYCFC, meanwhile, arrive in a very different situation. The visitors sit tenth in the Eastern Conference with 33 points and need results to keep their playoff hopes alive. They are coming off a 2-1 loss to Chicago Fire, which extended their winless run to three matches and has worsened the situation for Pascal Jansen’s side.




Midweek fútbol awaits. 🫡⚽️ #MIAvNYCFC🎟️ https://t.co/41vfglG4PF pic.twitter.com/JEscTtiGRd— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) October 12, 2026




Inter Miami dealing with one absence



Inter Miami will be without midfielder Yannick Bright for the match against NYCFC, as he is the club’s only confirmed absence. Bright has been sidelined with a foot injury since coming off after 40 minutes against Columbus Crew. Since he was unable to return to training in time, he was ruled out of the 4-0 win over D.C. United, and he remains unavailable for Wednesday’s showdown at Nu Stadium.


        


There is better news on the injury front for Messi and company, as Facundo Mura returns to the squad. The defender had been dealing with an ankle sprain since he was substituted in the 71st minute against Columbus, and he is back in the matchday group for the potential playoff-clinching game.



With the playoffs within reach, Inter Miami have a chance to take a big step toward the postseason at home, backed by an in-form attack and a squad that is nearly at full strength. Messi and Suárez will once again be the ones to watch, while NYCFC will try to keep their own playoff hopes alive and spoil the night in Miami.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo faces fresh UEFA Champions League goalscoring record threat as Harry Kane matches Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy
items.description:
The Bayern Munich striker's latest European performance has brought him closer to Ronaldo's long-standing record, setting up an intriguing challenge as the 2026-27 campaign unfolds. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has another reason to keep an eye on the UEFA Champions League, with Harry Kane matching the remarkable nine-game goalscoring streaks achieved by Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy. The Bayern Munich striker’s latest European performance has brought him closer to Ronaldo’s long-standing record, setting up an intriguing challenge as the 2026-27 campaign unfolds.



Kane reached the milestone during Bayern‘s dramatic 3-3 draw against Viking on Tuesday, October 13, scoring twice to help his team recover from a difficult start. Despite the Englishman’s impressive achievement, one of football’s greatest goalscorers remains ahead of him.



The Bundesliga champion endured a frustrating evening in Norway after Viking raced into a surprising 2-0 lead at Lyse Arena. Gianni Stensness opened the scoring in the second minute before Peter Christiansen doubled the home side’s advantage shortly before half-time.



The Englishman responded after the break, converting a penalty in the 54th minute before heading home a Joshua Kimmich cross six minutes later to make it 2-2. Luis Díaz subsequently put Bayern ahead, but Michael Olise’s red card in the 74th minute left the visitors with 10 men, allowing Kristoffer Haugen to equalize in the 90th minute.









Although the Bavarians failed to secure all three points, Kane‘s brace ensured that his extraordinary Champions League scoring streak continued. The 33-year-old has now scored in nine consecutive appearances in Europe’s premier club competition, placing him among an exclusive group of forwards.



Lewandowski and Van Nistelrooy reached the same milestone



Kane’s achievement also places him alongside two other celebrated strikers who enjoyed extraordinary consistency in Europe. Ruud van Nistelrooy scored in nine consecutive Champions League matches for Manchester United in 2002-03, while Lewandowski achieved the same feat twice with Bayern Munich.



The Polish striker’s runs came between September 2019 and August 2020, and again between November 2020 and November 2021. Lewandowski remains the only player to have recorded the nine-game sequence on two separate occasions, underlining his sustained excellence at the highest level.



Robert Lewandowski of FC Bayern Muenchen celebrates after scoring



According to UEFA, Kane became the fourth player to score in nine successive matches in the competition, joining Ronaldo, Van Nistelrooy and Lewandowski. His latest brace has therefore put him in elite company while keeping the record-holder firmly within reach.



How many goals to reach Ronaldo’s record?



The next milestone Kane is chasing belongs to Ronaldo, who scored in 11 consecutive Champions League matches during his time at Real Madrid in 2017 and 2018. The Portuguese superstar’s run began with two goals in Madrid’s 4-1 victory over Juventus in the 2017 final and continued throughout the following season’s group stage and knockout rounds.



GoalsPlayerClubSeason11Cristiano RonaldoReal Madrid2017–189Ruud van NistelrooyManchester United2002–039Robert LewandowskiBayern Munich2019–209Robert LewandowskiBayern Munich2020–219Harry KaneBayern Munich2026–present8Cristiano RonaldoReal Madrid2013–14



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner scored in all six group-stage matches before finding the net in both legs of Madrid’s round-of-16 tie against Paris Saint-Germain and both legs of their quarter-final against Juventus. He scored 17 goals across the 11-match sequence, establishing a benchmark that has remained unbeaten.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid celebrating.



Kane now needs to score in two more consecutive Champions League appearances to equal Ronaldo’s record. Another goal beyond that would give the Bayern forward sole possession of the mark, provided he maintains his streak without interruption.



9 – Only Cristiano Ronaldo in April 2018 (11) has enjoyed a longer run of successive games with a goal in the European Cup/UEFA Champions League than Harry Kane’s ongoing run of nine.

items.title: Harry Kane joins Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi among the Champions League’s all-time top 10 scorers
items.description:
Harry Kane scored a brace against Viking to join Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi in the Champions League’s all-time top 10 scorers. 
Harry Kane has joined an elite company in the Champions League record books. The Bayern Munich striker has entered the competition’s all-time top 10 scorers, a list headed by Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, after another goal-scoring night in Europe.



Kane scored a brace in Bayern’s 3-3 draw at Viking, lifting his Champions League tally from 55 to 57 goals. The brace puts him level with Thomas Muller in tenth place and ahead of Mohamed Salah and Thierry Henry.



The 33-year-old has found a second wind in the competition since moving to Bayern in 2023. He scored 21 goals in 32 Champions League appearances for Tottenham, and with the two against Viking he now has 36 in 40 games for the Bavarians.



Kane is also the highest-scoring English player in Champions League history, and he holds the record for most goals by an English player in a single campaign, with 14 in 2025/26. Even so, Ronaldo and Messi remain far ahead at the top.




Tonight’s player of the match 🏆 pic.twitter.com/lfMl4CuMCL— FC Bayern (@FCBayernEN) October 13, 2026




The Portuguese superstar leads with 141 goals, while the Argentine legend is second on 129, two totals that put Kane’s progress in perspective. Still, reaching the top 10 at this stage of his career shows how consistently the Englishman has delivered on Europe’s biggest stage.


        


Champions League all-time top 10 scorers



The list is led by Ronaldo and Messi, the only two players above 120 goals, followed by Robert Lewandowski, who is clear in third place with 109. Kylian Mbappe is level with Raul on 71 goals, while Erling Haaland, who is still chasing the leaders, shares 59 with Andriy Shevchenko.



PlayerGoalsCristiano Ronaldo141Lionel Messi129Robert Lewandowski109Karim Benzema90Raul71Kylian Mbappe71Ruud van Nistelrooy60Andriy Shevchenko59Erling Haaland59Harry Kane57Thomas Muller57



With the top four now outside the Champions League, the door is open for the players still active in Europe to climb the list. Ronaldo and Benzema find themselves in the Saudi Pro League with Al Nassr and Al Hilal respectively, while Lewandowski joined Chicago Fire to face Messi’s Inter Miami in MLS.



That leaves Mbappe, Haaland and Kane as the main contenders to chase them down. Mbappe, who is on 71 goals, needs 20 more to pass Benzema in fourth place, while Haaland and Kane, on 59 and 57, will need more time to close the gap on the leaders.

items.title: Why is Raphinha not playing for Barcelona vs Galatasaray in 2026-27 UEFA Champions League?
items.description:
The Brazilian forward’s absence comes at an inconvenient time for the Catalan side, which has made a perfect start to the season and will be looking to maintain its momentum in Europe. 
Raphinha will miss Barcelona’s crucial UEFA Champions League meeting with Galatasaray as Hansi Flick prepares his team for a demanding trip to Istanbul. The Brazilian forward’s absence comes at an inconvenient time for the Catalan side, which has made a perfect start to the season and will be looking to maintain its momentum in Europe.



Barcelona travel to RAMS Park on Tuesday, October 13, after winning all eight of their opening La Liga matches and beating Feyenoord 5-1 in their Champions League opener. Galatasaray, meanwhile, needs a positive result after losing 3-1 to Sporting CP in its first European fixture.



Flick’s side has been one of the most impressive teams in Europe during the opening weeks of the campaign. Barcelona’s latest 3-0 victory over Getafe extended its winning run in La Liga to eight matches, leaving the club with 24 points, 34 goals scored, and seven conceded.



The Catalan side also began its European campaign emphatically, defeating Feyenoord 5-1 at Camp Nou on September 9. Raphinha scored twice in that match, underscoring the attacking threat the Blaugrana will miss against Galatasaray.









Despite his absence, Flick still has several quality options available in the final third. Gabriel Jesus is expected to lead the attack, with Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon providing width and creativity, while Pedri and Rodri will be important to Barcelona’s efforts to control possession.



Why is Raphinha missing against Galatasaray?



Raphinha is unavailable due to a muscle injury in the back of his right thigh sustained while playing for Brazil during the international break. He was substituted at half-time during Brazil’s 4-2 friendly victory over Australia on September 29 before returning to Barcelona for medical examinations.



The initial findings offered some encouragement because they did not indicate a major muscle tear. However, Barcelona remained cautious because Raphinha had suffered three muscle injuries during the previous season, raising concerns about the risk of another setback if he returned too soon.



Raphinha of FC Barcelona Interacts with Hansi Flick, Manager of FC Barcelona



Flick explained the club’s approach ahead of the Galatasaray fixture. “The picture showed something, but it’s not a big injury,” the Barcelona manager said, according to The Athletic. He added: “It’s something we have to take care of because last season he had three injuries there. He won’t be eligible tomorrow, nor in Istanbul either.”



Why Raphinha missed Getafe and Galatasaray



Barcelona’s schedule following the international break left little time for Raphinha to complete his recovery. He was unavailable for the La Liga match against Getafe on October 10 and has also been ruled out of the Champions League trip to Galatasaray on October 13. The two absences are part of the same recovery period rather than separate injury setbacks.



Barcelona’s priority is to ensure that the Brazilian can return to full training without aggravating the problem. His absence is significant because Raphinha has become an important part of Flick’s attacking system. His pressing, movement and ability to create chances give Barcelona an additional dimension, particularly in matches when opponents defend deep.



Raphinha of FC Barcelona celebrates scoring



When could Raphinha return?



Raphinha’s next possible appearances depend on how quickly he progresses through rehabilitation and resumes full training. Barcelona faces Real Betis on October 17, followed by a Champions League meeting with Paris Saint-Germain on October 20 and El Clasico against Real Madrid on October 25.



The PSG fixture has emerged as a potential target for his return, but it should not be treated as a confirmed comeback date. Barcelona president Joan Laporta reportedly offered encouragement when discussing the winger’s recovery, saying: “The doctors say he’ll be available for the match in Paris.”



That assessment suggests the club is hopeful Raphinha will be ready for the trip to France. His availability will ultimately depend on his medical progress and whether he can return to training without discomfort.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr make urgent request ahead of Al-Ahli clash in Saudi Pro League as travel issue emerges
items.description:
With the match scheduled for Thursday, October 15, uncertainty surrounding the team’s travel plans has raised questions about whether the high-profile encounter can proceed as planned. 
Cristiano Ronaldo and Al-Nassr face an unexpected challenge ahead of one of the Saudi Pro League’s most anticipated fixtures, with the club seeking urgent changes to its preparations for the upcoming clash against Al-Ahli. With the match scheduled for Thursday, October 15, uncertainty surrounding the team’s travel plans has raised questions about whether the high-profile encounter can proceed as planned.



The situation has developed following a demanding week for Al-Nassr, which played in continental competition in Riyadh before turning its attention to a crucial domestic fixture in Jeddah. The club is now waiting for a decision that could significantly affect its preparation and recovery time.



Ronaldo’s side has formally requested that the Saudi Pro League postpone its match against Al-Ahli, according to reports from Rotana Sport and other Saudi media outlets. The fixture is scheduled for Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 9 p.m. local time in Jeddah, but the club has yet to receive confirmation that the request will be accepted.



The uncertainty has also affected the team’s immediate plans. According to reports attributed to Ali Alabdallah and other accounts covering the club, Al-Nassr had not departed Riyadh while awaiting further developments, with its delegation reportedly prepared to travel if the match remained on schedule.



🚨 CRISTIANO RONALDO SCORES GOAL NUMBER 981 A TURN AND VOLLEY 🥶 pic.twitter.com/lk9ReEtkJh— Baller HQ (@FootballerHQ) October 12, 2026 



The travel problem behind the postponement request



The main issue is disruption to air travel from Riyadh, which could force Al-Nassr to make an approximately 11-hour journey by road to Jeddah. Such a trip would leave the players with less time to recover and prepare for a match that carries significant implications for the league standings.



The problem comes after an exhausting continental fixture on Monday, October 12. Al-Nassr’s 3-1 AFC Champions League Elite victory over Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana was reportedly delayed by around an hour following a security alert in Riyadh linked to a missile threat attributed to Houthi forces.



The alert prompted a Civil Defense warning and disrupted the evening’s preparations. The 41-year-old veteran featured in the victory, but the late finish and subsequent travel uncertainty have complicated the club’s preparations for its next match.



Cristiano Ronaldo of team Al Nassr celebrates scoring



Why the Al-Ahli clash matters



The encounter is widely regarded as one of the Saudi Pro League’s major fixtures, often described as a clasico because of the stature of the two clubs. Al-Nassr sits third with 19 points from eight matches, while Al-Ahli occupies sixth place with 15 points.



Both clubs have ambitions of challenging near the top of the table, making the timing of the fixture particularly important. Al-Nassr will want to maintain its momentum after the continental victory, while Al-Ahli will look to take advantage of playing at home.



A long journey immediately before the match could affect Al-Nassr’s energy levels and preparation. The club’s request therefore raises a wider question about how leagues should respond when exceptional circumstances interfere with player recovery and scheduled travel.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s attendance at the Ballon d’Or gala in London reportedly remains unconfirmed
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s attendance at the Ballon d’Or gala in London remains unconfirmed less than two weeks before the October 26 ceremony. 
Lionel Messi’s presence at the 2026 Ballon d’Or gala in London is still up in the air, with his attendance reportedly yet to be confirmed and no role in the trophy presentation planned for him. The uncertainty comes less than two weeks before the October 26 ceremony, where the eight-time winner is among this year’s nominees.



According to Fabrizio Romano, Messi will not be presenting a trophy to any of the winners, as he has not been invited to do so, and his attendance at the gala has not yet been confirmed. 



The update goes against earlier reports that had placed the Argentine at the center of the night, with some outlets claiming he would attend with his family and even hand the golden trophy to the new winner.



Messi earned his place among the 30 nominees thanks to a campaign that included Inter Miami’s first MLS Cup title in 2025, a season in which he won the Golden Boot with 29 goals and a second straight MVP award.



Lionel Messi #10 of Inter Miami CF lifts the MLS Cup trophy. (Getty Images)



He then led Argentina to the 2026 World Cup final, where he scored eight goals and added four assists before the Albiceleste fell 1-0 to Spain. It is the 17th Ballon d’Or nomination of his career, and whether he ends up in London, and in what role, remains to be seen.


        


Why is the Ballon d’Or being held in London?



Unlike previous editions, which were staged in Paris, the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony will cross the Channel and take place in London for the first time in the award’s history. The change of venue is more than a logistical decision, as it carries a symbolic meaning tied to the origins of the prize itself.



The 70th edition of the award will take place at the London Palladium on October 26, marking the first time the Ballon d’Or is presented in the English capital. The change of venue is a symbolic choice to honor Sir Stanley Matthews, who became the first winner of the prize in 1956.



Matthews, then a Blackpool winger, was 41 when he received the inaugural trophy from France Football, making him one of the most enduring figures in English football history. Seventy years later, the ceremony will leave its usual home in Paris to pay tribute to the man who started the tradition.

items.title: Thibaut Courtois set to extend Real Madrid stay past 2027 after reportedly reaching agreement
items.description:
Thibaut Courtois has been an essential pillar for Real Madrid since joining the club in 2018, and Los Blancos have now reached an agreement in principle to extend his contract beyond June 2027. 
Real Madrid found in Thibaut Courtois one of the most reliable goalkeepers in recent soccer history. Now, the club has reportedly decided to keep him for longer, extending his contract beyond 2027.



In 2018, Real Madrid made a blockbuster move by signing Thibaut Courtois. Despite a highly successful run with Keylor Navas, Los Blancos wanted a smooth transition with the Costa Rican set to leave the club soon.



Courtois lived up to expectations and has become a key player for the club ever since. His current contract expires in June 2027, but according to Fabrizio Romano, it will be extended through the 2027–28 season.



Uncertainty regarding the future of the position



Despite the recent challenges Real Madrid have faced, Thibaut Courtois has remained a vital figure for the Spanish club and is regarded as a crucial element of the squad despite managerial changes.



Thibaut Courtois of Real Madrid acknowledges the fans.



The 34-year-old goalkeeper earns around $17 million per season. His new deal is expected to feature similar terms, but the duration of the extension is what has drawn attention from supporters.


        


With reports indicating that only one year will be added to his current deal, it suggests Real Madrid may be planning for a transition in goal by June 2028, leaving many to wonder who will eventually succeed him in such a critical role.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo scores 981st career goal: Can he reach the 1,000-goal mark before 2027?
items.description:
Cristiano Ronaldo keeps adding goals to his career. Now that he has scored the 981st goal in his tally, could he reach the 1,000-goal mark before the year ends? 
Cristiano Ronaldo keeps scoring, and the 1,000-goal mark seems more reachable than ever. However, after netting the 981st goal of his career, many are wondering whether he could reach that historic milestone before 2027.



On Matchday 2 of the 2026–27 AFC Champions League Elite, Cristiano Ronaldo scored Al Nassr‘s second goal against Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana—marking the 981st goal of his career.



He is now just 19 goals away from the 1,000-goal threshold, and at his current pace, he could potentially reach the milestone before the new year begins.



Road to 1,000 goals: Mathematical breakdown for Cristiano Ronaldo



A total of 19 goals is all that Cristiano Ronaldo needs to hit 1,000 career goals. Fortunately, he has plenty of fixtures remaining before the year ends to try to reach that mark by December.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



Al Nassr has 15 matches remaining on their schedule this year. Combined with international duty for Portugal—where he is set to return in November—he will have two additional games to build on his tally.


        


If everything goes as expected, he will have 17 matches available. While he may not feature in every single one, assuming full availability, he would need to score at least a brace in two matches and a single goal in the remaining 15 to hit the 1,000-goal mark before the new year.



Obviously, scoring 19 goals in 17 games would require a monumental effort from Ronaldo. However, even if he falls short, he will still have the first half of 2027 during the remainder of the season to reach and surpass the milestone.



Recent history is not on his side



During the 2025–26 season, Cristiano Ronaldo averaged 0.82 goals per match, a figure well below the scoring rate required to reach the 1,000-goal mark before 2026 concludes.



Nevertheless, his main objective will be to close the gap as much as possible before 2027, reducing the pressure as he enters the second half of the campaign.

items.title: Why was Al Nassr vs Neftchi Fergana kickoff delayed at 2026-27 AFC Champions League Elite?
items.description:
The game between Al Nassr and Neftchi Fergana in Matchday 2 of the 2026-27 AFC Champions League Elite suffered a delay in the kickoff time due to problems in Riyadh. 
The AFC Champions League Elite fixture between Al Nassr and Neftchi Fergana at Al-Awwal Park in Riyadh was officially postponed following heightened security alerts in the Saudi Arabian capital. Match officials halted pre-game preparations after regional air defense activity and a missile strike in the wider Riyadh metropolitan area triggered emergency security protocols surrounding the stadium, as reported by Ryan Rozbiani.



In response to the safety advisory, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and local organizers intervened to suspend stadium operations, prioritizing the well-being of players, coaching staff, and spectators. Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana and their traveling delegation, who had landed in Riyadh via charter flight ahead of the contest, remained in safe isolation at their hotel while awaiting formal updates from tournament officials.



Competition administrators are currently reviewing logistical options to determine when the group stage encounter will be played. Potential solutions under discussion between football authorities and both clubs include rescheduling the fixture for a later date or relocating the match to a neutral venue to ensure it can be conducted safely.



Will the game be played?



According to authorities, the game has been delayed due to missile strikes targeting Riyadh. The match was scheduled to be played at Al-Awwal Park, located in the capital city.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



Reports indicate that kickoff initially suffered a 30-minute delay, but that revised time has already passed. Announcements over the stadium public address system instructed fans inside the venue to remain calm, stay in their seats, and await further official updates.


        


As of now, The Nassr Tribune reports that the game will start at 10:15 PM Saudi time (3:15 PM ET). Although Al-Awwal Park has not suffered any direct hits, authorities decided to delay it due to any potential problems.

items.description:
Al Nassr host Uzbekistan's Neftchi Fergana in Matchday 2 of the 2026–27 AFC Champions League Elite at Al-Awwal Park, with the primary question surrounding the availability and status of captain Cristiano Ronaldo. 
Al Nassr face a crucial match in the 2026–27 AFC Champions League Elite as they host Uzbekistan’s Neftchi Fergana. The big question remaining is whether Cristiano Ronaldo will play for the Saudi side.



Cristiano Ronaldo will start for Al Nassr on Matchday 2 of the 2026–27 AFC Champions League Elite. He participated in his club’s recent Saudi Pro League win over Diriyah Club, opening the scoring in his team’s 3–0 victory.



Head coach Ange Postecoglou recently provided an update on Cristiano Ronaldo’s status, confirming that the striker was set to start against the Uzbek side in a vital encounter for Al Nassr.



Al Nassr’s confirmed lineup



Al Nassr enter this continental clash eager to bounce back following a defeat to Al Ain on opening night. Securing all three points is vital for the Saudi side as they aim to climb out of the bottom of the standings.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr.



Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Bento Matheus Krepski; Nawaf Boushal, Mohamed Simakan, Íñigo Martínez, Awad Aman; Ângelo Gabriel, Samú Costa, Kingsley Coman; Sadio Mané, João Félix, Cristiano Ronaldo. Coach: Ange Postecoglou.


        


Neftchi Fergana’s confirmed lineup



As for Neftchi Fergana, they earned a win on Matchday 1 and currently occupy a playoff spot. While plenty of fixtures remain in the campaign, getting off on the right foot—and potentially claiming a landmark victory on the road against Al Nassr—could prove crucial in their quest to advance to the next round.



Neftchi Fergana confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Botirali Ergashev; Ibrohimkhalil Yuldoshev, Bojan Ciger, Michel Augusto, Anvar G’ofurov, Koffi Kouao; Yan Sasse, Ikromjon Alibaev, Jamshid Iskanderov, Abrorbek Ismoilov; Marcus Forss. Coach: Islombek Ismoilov.
